SA3f-36.claim: Diplomatic sources said in September 2026 that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman might visit Riyadh in the second half of November 2026 at the invitation of Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, with strengthening bilateral relations, energy imports, investment agreements, regional and international issues and continued Saudi support on the Rohingya question as possible topics.
SA3f-36.why_new: Upcoming high-level visit where stranded-visa or labour issues could be raised; low priority for the doc.

SA3f-37.claim: On 4 October 2026 a Houthi missile or drone hit an Aramco facility at Al Khurais in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and killed Bangladeshi worker Md Sajib Hossain (26) of Brahmanpara, Cumilla; the Foreign Ministry said the embassy had contacted his family and employer and was coordinating with the Saudi authorities to send his body home.
SA3f-37.why_new: The guide's status line mentions attacks on airports only; workers at oil facilities have also been killed.

SA3f-38.claim: For Sajib Hossain, killed in Saudi Arabia in October 2026, the Brahmanpara UNO said his father and brother, who also lived in Saudi Arabia, would lead the effort to bring his body home.
SA3f-38.target_section: If a worker dies in Saudi Arabia
SA3f-38.why_new: Shows relatives on the Saudi side handling repatriation; minor.
SA3f-38.h2: If a worker dies, is injured or loses the job

SA3f-39.claim: From January to 30 September 2026, 4,060 bodies of migrant workers reached Bangladesh, more than 14 a day, the article reports, while Wage Earners' Welfare Board data show 3,651 bodies came home in 2019 and 3,140 in 2020.
SA3f-39.target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: How is the body brought home?
SA3f-39.why_new: National death numbers; not in either guide. 8cd6aabe prints 4,064 for the same period.

SA3f-40.claim: About 2,000 Bangladeshi workers died in Saudi Arabia in 2026 up to the end of September, more than in any other country, Prothom Alo reported; the head of BRAC's Migration Programme said over 70% of bodies come from the Middle East, most from Saudi Arabia, and that young men aged 25 to 30 are also dying.
SA3f-40.target_section: If a worker dies in Saudi Arabia
SA3f-40.why_new: The guide has no Saudi death figure.
SA3f-40.h2: If a worker dies, is injured or loses the job

SA3f-41.claim: By the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry's data, the papers with returned bodies gave the cause as natural death in 66% of cases in January to September 2026, against about 70% before, and more than 16% died in road or work accidents, fires, falls from buildings or electrocution; the minister said on 1 October 2026 that steps to verify causes of death abroad would be decided.
SA3f-41.target_section: If a worker dies in Saudi Arabia
SA3f-41.why_new: Adds numbers to the guide's statement that the cause is usually recorded as natural and not checked [E0093]; all destinations, not Saudi only.
SA3f-41.h2: If a worker dies, is injured or loses the job

SA3f-42.claim: Welfare Board officials said in October 2026 that bodies from Middle Eastern countries need approval from several offices before they can be sent, which takes some time though less than before, and that outside pandemic years under 1% of migrants who die are buried in the destination country.
SA3f-42.target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: How is the body brought home?
SA3f-42.why_new: Why repatriation from the Gulf takes time; burial-abroad share is new.

SA3f-43.claim: Brothers Foyez Ahmed, ten years in Saudi Arabia, and Sujon Ahmed, who had joined him seven months earlier, of Noakhali, who carried dates in the same vehicle, died in a road accident on 16 July 2026; their bodies reached Bangladesh on 28 July and the Welfare Board paid Tk 35,000 each for burial, their father said.
SA3f-43.target_section: If a worker dies in Saudi Arabia
SA3f-43.why_new: Real timeline (12 days) and confirmation that the Tk 35,000 burial payment is paid per body in 2026 (cross-country doc asks whether it is Tk 35,000 or Tk 25,000).
SA3f-43.h2: If a worker dies, is injured or loses the job

SA3f-44.claim: By Welfare Board data, in the first six months of 2026 it paid Tk 9.45 crore for burial, Tk 61.56 crore in grants and more than Tk 44 crore in insurance, and recovered about Tk 75 crore in compensation, unpaid wages and insurance from abroad; people in the sector said families must visit the Board day after day after applying.
SA3f-44.target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: If a worker dies abroad, what does the family get?
SA3f-44.why_new: Board payout volumes for 2026; the guide notes families chase repeatedly [E0092].

SA3f-45.claim: In a Welfare Board analysis of 2018 to 2022, 18,166 bodies came home, of which 3,698 died in road accidents, workplace accidents, fires, falls from buildings or electric shock, 2,649 of them in road accidents.
SA3f-45.target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: How is the body brought home?
SA3f-45.why_new: Cause breakdown over five years. The editorial a5cf655e gives the same 18,166 for '2018 to 2023'.

SA3f-46.claim: Migration research bodies said in October 2026 that a large share of Bangladeshi workers in the Middle East work in construction in extreme daytime heat, which can damage the kidneys, brain and other organs, worsen breathing, heart, diabetes and kidney disease, and cause premature death.
SA3f-46.why_new: Health risk behind the guide's summer midday work ban (Hours section); not Saudi-specific.

SA3f-47.claim: Expatriates' Welfare Ministry officials said in October 2026 that BMET's pre-departure training is only a three-day workshop in which nothing is taught well, and that workers need training on the destination's type of work, conditions, working hours and staying healthy.
SA3f-47.target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What is the pre-departure orientation (PDO)?
SA3f-47.why_new: Ministry officials' own view of the PDO; the cross-country doc has similar views from a federation and UNDP expert.

SA3f-48.claim: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir said on 10 October 2026 that Bangladesh was in positive talks with Saudi Arabia on sending skilled and professional workers, and that Bangladesh had already expressed interest in joining the Makkah defence agreement.
SA3f-48.why_new: Status of talks on skilled-worker recruitment; no details or dates were given.

SA3f-49.claim: At 3:20 pm local time on 10 October 2026 a Houthi missile hit Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, where passengers from Bangladesh and other countries were waiting, killing two Bangladeshis, according to the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry.
SA3f-49.why_new: The guide mentions Houthi attacks on airports but no casualties; the embassy's labour wing put the time at about 3:15 pm (3c48fdff).

SA3f-50.claim: One of the two Bangladeshis killed in the 10 October 2026 Riyadh airport attack, Md Shahed Ahmmad of Bogura, a plumber with an iqama on a Saudi contractor's Jeddah project, was returning to work through Riyadh after leave in Bangladesh; the other, Md Nasrullah Badarpuri of Cumilla, was an Umrah pilgrim waiting to fly from Riyadh to Jeddah.
SA3f-50.target_section: Going home on leave and coming back
SA3f-50.why_new: Shows the risk on the Riyadh transit route that workers and pilgrims use to reach Jeddah.

SA3f-51.claim: Of the 24 Bangladeshis injured in the 10 October 2026 Riyadh airport attack, 11 worked in Saudi Arabia and 13 had come on Umrah visas, according to Foreign Ministry sources citing the embassy, and the embassy was in touch with the hospitals to secure their treatment.
SA3f-51.why_new: Umrah pilgrims routed via Riyadh were among the casualties; the embassy's later count was 27 injured, 16 on Umrah visas (3c48fdff, 8cd6aabe).

SA3f-52.claim: After the 10 October 2026 attack about 500 Bangladeshi passengers were stranded at Riyadh airport; the embassy, with the airport authority, Saudi immigration and the airlines, arranged hotel rooms, food and onward travel, including a special bus to Jeddah for 67 Umrah pilgrims in ihram, flights home via King Fahd airport in Dammam for about 400 passengers of the cancelled Saudia flight SV804, and the Al Khobar land border crossing for two Bahrain-bound workers.
SA3f-52.why_new: Evidence of what the embassy actually did for stranded passengers; the guide's status line has no such detail.

SA3f-53.claim: In an urgent notice on 12 October 2026 the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh said that recording, exchanging or posting on social media any information, photo or video about the ongoing Middle East situation is a punishable offence under Saudi law, and asked Bangladeshis not to post such material on Facebook, YouTube, X or other platforms, nor keep it on their phones or share it.
SA3f-53.target_section: What can get you jailed or deported
SA3f-53.why_new: Partly answers the guide's Need to know on which online acts are crimes; the guide has nothing on filming attacks.

SA3f-54.claim: On 12 October 2026 the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh asked Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia to stay alert, follow Saudi authorities' instructions and avoid risky and crowded places; flights were halted that day at two Saudi airports including King Khalid in Riyadh, and the US, Canada, the UK, South Korea, Japan, Australia and New Zealand issued travel advisories for Saudi Arabia.
SA3f-54.why_new: The embassy's safety notice; the hotlines it listed match the guide's Contacts.

SA3f-55.claim: The embassy labour wing's report on the 10 October 2026 Riyadh airport attack put the dead at 13 of various nationalities, including two Bangladeshis, and 309 injured, including 27 Bangladeshis (11 workers and 16 on Umrah visas), of whom 15 were in hospital and one, an Umrah pilgrim from Naogaon, was critical.
SA3f-55.why_new: Conflicts within Prothom Alo reporting: other articles give 12 dead and 24 Bangladeshis injured (198bf3f6, 43568e1a); this is the embassy's later count.

SA3f-56.claim: After the 10 October 2026 Riyadh airport attack, the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh said late on 12 October that restrictions at Saudi airports had hit 61 flights between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia, direct and transit, some cancelled and some suspended, affecting 8,381 passengers due to fly from Dhaka; Biman suspended all Dhaka-Riyadh flights until 17 October and US-Bangla cancelled its Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights until 21 October, and some Dhaka-Jeddah flights were also cancelled.
SA3f-56.why_new: Dated detail behind the guide's flight-disruption line; the CAAB breakdown as printed (12 direct, 39 transit; direct by airline 9+2+4+7) doesn't add up.

SA3f-57.claim: Members of BAIRA (the recruiting agencies' association) and BMET sources said that in 2026 about 1,200 new workers a day went to Saudi Arabia and 600 to 700 a day returned after leave, and by that reckoning about 5,500 workers would have been stranded by three days of flight disruption in October 2026.
SA3f-57.why_new: Daily flow figures and the scale of stranding; not in the guide.

SA3f-58.claim: State Minister Md Nurul Haque said in October 2026 that the government would hold talks to arrange travel for stranded workers and that visa validity had been extended automatically earlier, at the start of the Middle East war; former BAIRA secretary general Ali Haider Chowdhury said visas of stranded workers had been renewed during the Kuwait war and the Covid pandemic.
SA3f-58.why_new: Partly answers the guide's Need to know on whether Saudi Arabia extended stranded workers' visas: an automatic extension happened at the war's start, but nothing was agreed for October.

SA3f-59.claim: By BMET figures, clearances for Saudi Arabia up to 12 October fell from 572,054 in 2025 to 311,567 in 2026, about 46%, and in the first 12 days of October alone from 3,971 to 1,850; the article also reports that about 6.25 lakh Bangladeshis went to Saudi Arabia for work in 2024 and more than 7.55 lakh in 2025.
SA3f-59.why_new: Consistent with the guide's 315,935 to 17 October (45% down) [E0129]; adds the 2024 figure and the October collapse.

SA3f-60.claim: By Expatriates' Welfare Ministry sources, 14 Bangladeshis had been killed in attacks in the Middle East from the start of the 2026 war to 12 October 2026, 8 of them registered as migrant workers.
SA3f-60.target_section: If a worker dies in Saudi Arabia
SA3f-60.why_new: War deaths are new; region-wide, not Saudi only.
SA3f-60.h2: If a worker dies, is injured or loses the job

SA3f-61.claim: Abul Hossain of Senbag, Noakhali, a tile mason six years in Saudi Arabia, had booked his return ticket three months ahead but his 12 October 2026 Biman flight to Dammam was cancelled, and he said that if he could not go back he would struggle to keep his job.
SA3f-61.target_section: Going home on leave and coming back
SA3f-61.why_new: Shows the risk to workers on leave when flights stop; the guide's leave section says nothing about that.

SA3f-62.claim: State Minister Md Nurul Haque said in October 2026 that the Saudi situation meant the target of sending 15 lakh workers in the government's first year would probably not be met, and that work on alternative labour markets continued.
SA3f-62.why_new: Government's own expectation for the corridor; minor.
